name: Launch Complex 39A
tagline: Launched all Apollo lunar missions; today flies Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, and Crew Dragon
dispatch: Launch Complex 39A was built around an idea nearly as radical as the rocket it served: don't build the rocket at the pad. Instead, stack the Saturn V inside the cavernous Vehicle Assembly Building, then carry the whole ~3,000-tonne stack out to the pad — standing upright — on a crawler-transporter creeping along at walking pace. That "clean pad" approach let one site turn around the largest rocket ever flown far faster than assembling it in place ever could. The design outlived Apollo by half a century: the same pad launched most of the Space Shuttle fleet and, leased to SpaceX in 2014, now flies Falcon Heavy and astronauts on Crew Dragon. Good infrastructure, it turns out, is the quietest kind of moonshot — build it once and it keeps paying off.
description: Built for Saturn V, kept for the Shuttle, leased to SpaceX in 2014. From Pad A: Apollo 4 (the first Saturn V), Apollo 11 (the first lunar landing), Apollo 13, Apollo 17 (the last lunar landing), Skylab, eighty-two Space Shuttle flights including the first STS-1, and since 2017 every Falcon Heavy and every Crew Dragon to the ISS. The same flame trench, the same crawlerway, three eras of US human spaceflight.
best_known_for: Launched all Apollo lunar missions; today flies Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, and Crew Dragon
